paragraphs.text: On 9 April 2025 a rent increase form for my flat at Sonnenweg 14 in Bern turned up in my letterbox, signed at Bern on 12 March 2025 by Claudia Vogt of Rietberg Immobilien AG. It lifts my net rent from CHF 1,640 to CHF 1,792 from 1 July 2025 and justifies this with a reference interest rate table that, as far as I can see, only came into force on 1 April 2025 - roughly three weeks after she signed.

When I queried the dates, the office sent me a printout of their processing history for the form by email. Ms Vogt then told me a few days later that the version numbers and save times in that printout had been pulled from the wrong system and had since been put right.

I also still have the letter about the rate that they keep pointing to. Whether it is the same document the form relies on or something else the office posted to me in April, I genuinely could not say.

What I would like looked at is whether a rate that only took effect after the signature can carry this increase, and whether the starting figures used for my rent are really the ones from my lease of 1 May 2021. What stays unclear to me is when the office actually finished preparing the form, because the dates I have been given so far do not line up with each other.

Before the current decision is taken, three facts must be on the record: the date the increase form was signed, the exact rate table relied on together with the period for which it applies, and the moment the completed form content was prepared. These are established by the signed increase notice showing the form date and the rate or table it cites, the publication excerpt for that table and its period of effect, and the property manager's workflow or audit log covering preparation of the completed form content; alternatively, an authenticated administrative export covering the notice, the table reference and the preparation history may be relied on. A party's account or recollection of what a record says does not establish its content - the record itself, or the authenticated export, is required.

The starting calculation basis tied to this notice must likewise be on the record before the matter is decided. This is established by the calculation worksheet setting out the starting basis used for the notice. However confidently either side describes that worksheet, a description or recollection does not establish its content; the worksheet itself, or the authenticated export, is required.

A renovation cost breakdown supporting a value-added increase comes into play only once the notice itself reveals a renovation reason. Do not request that breakdown unless a returned signed increase notice reports the triggering circumstance; until it does, the obligation stays dormant.

Current rent-payment receipts are not required for this check and should not be requested. Readiness here means that the listed facts are established from the required records; it does not decide whether the increase is legally owed.

What struck me straight away was the signature date of 4 March 2025, because the 1.75 per cent reference interest rate the form leans on was only made public in June.

My own reading of the form is quite clear: the manager's signature line shows 4 March 2025, and the rate quoted just above it is 1.75 per cent. Martin Roth at Brunner Immobilien AG tells me I am misremembering, and that the copy sitting in their file carries a June signature date alongside the same rate. One of us has the order of events wrong, and I cannot settle that from memory alone.

During a phone call on 18 August 2025, Mr Roth mentioned that their system keeps a record of when the wording of the notice was actually put together, and he said it would reach me on its own within the next few days. I never asked him for it; he described sending that record out as ordinary office routine.

Sorting through the folder in my hallway cupboard on 20 August 2025, I came across the worksheet setting out the starting figures behind the increase. It is here with me and I can pass it on the moment you want it, though I have made no attempt to interpret what it says.

Could you please look at whether a rent increase may rest on a reference rate that only came into existence after the form had been signed? I genuinely do not know which date is the one that counts here: the date under the signature, the day the office finished drafting the form, or the day the rate itself became applicable.

What struck me straight away was that the space where a reason belongs had simply been left empty. A week later, on 24 March, Ms. Frei of Rueegg Verwaltungs AG wrote to me by e-mail that this was "a normal market adjustment", and that one line is the only explanation I have been given.

At the tenants' information evening on 21 January 2025, Mr. Bruderer of Hofmatt Immobilien AG told us quite plainly that the 2024 refurbishment had been covered out of the renovation fund and that no statement of those costs would be passed on to us. The management now insists that a detailed statement of the renovation costs, separating upkeep from value-adding work, went to every household in December 2024; I never saw such a sheet, and my neighbour on the same floor says the same.

I went through my folder again yesterday evening, and the signed adjustment form itself is here at home, along with the envelope it arrived in. I can put it in the post to you tomorrow or scan it this afternoon, whichever suits you better. I would rather not paraphrase what it says, because I am obviously not reading it the way the management does.

Then there is the letter I keep coming back to, the one that shows when all of this was actually put together in their office. I am no longer sure whether that is the same document the management pointed to during our telephone call on 2 April 2025, and I do not want to guess at it.

What I would like looked at now is whether an increase of CHF 165 a month can stand at all when the form itself names no reason and the only explanation arrived afterwards by e-mail. What genuinely remains unclear to me is which of the two counts: the empty space on the form, or Ms. Frei's market-adjustment sentence of 24 March 2025.

paragraphs.text: The rent adjustment form for my flat at Lindenweg 12 in Bern is dated 14 March 2025 and landed in my letterbox four days later, and ever since I have been given two different stories about the renovation money. At the tenants' meeting on 2 April 2025, Ms Egger of Bergmann Immobilien AG told me face to face that the cantonal subsidy of CHF 140,000 had already been taken off the renovation costs before anything was passed on to us, whereas the letter that reached me from the same office on 28 April 2025 says the subsidy was booked against the owner's own contribution and changed nothing at all for me. My net rent is meant to climb from CHF 1,680 to CHF 1,915 on 1 October 2025.

When I rang the cantonal publication office on 6 May 2025 to ask about the rate table my increase points to, the clerk told me I did not need to put in a request at all. Their office sends the published extract, with the table and the dates it covers, out on its own initiative, and she said it should be in the post to me within a few days.

Over the weekend I dug through the folder where I keep everything to do with the flat, and the certified administrative export that Bergmann Immobilien had drawn up for this increase is sitting in it, seal and all, covering the notice, the table it refers to and the preparation history. I have it here at home and can pass it on to you whenever you want it; I have not worked my way through what it records.

The calculation sheet I was shown at the meeting I still remember reasonably well: it began from a net rent of CHF 1,680 with 1 July 2021 marked as the date that basis was set, and it put the reference rate at that time at 1.25 per cent. That is going purely on what I saw on the screen that evening.

What I would like looked at now is whether the increase taking effect on 1 October 2025 was really worked out the way the form says, and above all whether the CHF 140,000 subsidy ought to have reduced the amount passed on to me. What I genuinely cannot work out on my own is which of the two statements from Bergmann Immobilien is the one that counts, the spoken one from the April meeting or the written one from the end of that month.

Three points must be settled before the current question is addressed: the date carried on the signed increase form, the exact rate or calculation table the form relies on together with the period that table covers, and the moment at which the content of the form was completed. These follow from the signed increase notice showing the form date and the referenced rate or table, the publication extract for that rate or table with its period of effect, and the workflow or audit log recording when the form content was prepared; an authenticated administrative export covering the notice, the table reference and the preparation history stands in place of that set. What a party remembers or reports about a document does not establish its content, so the document itself, or the authenticated export, must be on file.

The starting calculation basis tied to this notice has to be established before the current question is decided. Only the calculation worksheet showing the basis actually used for the notice will establish it. A description or recollection of that worksheet from either side does not establish what it contains; the worksheet itself, or the authenticated export, is required.

The renovation cost breakdown is a conditional item. It comes into play solely once a returned signed increase notice itself reports that the increase rests on a renovation reason; until such a notice has come in and says so, do not ask the property manager for the renovation cost breakdown supporting a value-added increase.

Current rent-payment receipts are not needed for this check and should not be requested for it. Readiness here means the listed facts are established from the documents required above; it decides nothing about whether the increase is legally owed.

paragraphs.text: When the rent adjustment landed in my letterbox on 14 March 2025, I rang Brunnenhof Verwaltung AG and was told quite plainly that the cantonal renovation subsidy had already been taken off the works costs before anything was passed on to us tenants. Two weeks later, on 28 March 2025, a colleague of his in the same office told me the opposite: the subsidy money sits in a separate building account and was never set against the renovation costs. I have been going back and forth between those two answers ever since.

From reading the published rate table at the counter I remember the figure 1.75 per cent, and it was marked as applying from 3 March 2025 onward. That is my recollection rather than something I have in front of me, but I am fairly confident about the date, because I noticed it was only nine days before the date on my own form.

On the telephone in April someone at the administration told me a certified export had been produced covering my notice, the table it refers to and the editing history behind it, and I wrote down 8 April 2025 as the day it was generated. Brunnenhof Verwaltung AG now insists that no certified export of that kind was ever made and that I am confusing it with an ordinary printout. One of those two accounts must be wrong, and I have no way of telling which.

Herr Tobias Frei, who runs their office, told me I would not have to chase anyone for it. According to him, the workflow and editing record for my notice is generated as a matter of course and will reach me within the next few working days without any request from my side.

What I would like looked at now is whether the step from CHF 1,940 to CHF 2,045 as from 1 October 2025 was built up correctly in the first place, given that the form itself carries the date 12 March 2025. What I still cannot work out is which rate table was genuinely in force at the moment the wording of my notice was settled, and whether the subsidy ever came off the cost side at all.

Three points must be on record before the present question is decided: the date borne by the signed increase form, the exact rate or calculation table relied on together with the period it covers, and the moment at which the wording of the notice was completed. Establish them from the signed increase form showing its own date and the rate or table it cites, from the published excerpt for that rate or table with its effective period, and from the workflow or audit record showing when the notice wording was completed; a certified administrative export covering the notice, the table reference and the preparation history may take the place of that workflow or audit record. What either side remembers or reports about a record does not establish its content — the record itself, or the certified export, is required.

The starting calculation basis tied to this notice must likewise be on record before the present question is answered, and it is established by the calculation worksheet setting out the basis actually used for the notice. However precise a party's account of that worksheet may sound, a description does not establish what the worksheet contains; the worksheet itself, or the certified administrative export, is needed.

The renovation cost breakdown is a conditional item rather than a standing one. It becomes an active obligation only if a returned signed increase form itself states a renovation-related ground for the adjustment; for as long as no such form is on record showing that ground, do not request a breakdown of renovation costs supporting a value-added increase.

Current rent-payment receipts are not needed for this check and should not be called in for it. Readiness here means only that the listed facts are established from the required records; it decides nothing about whether the increase is legally owed.

paragraphs.text: Am Dienstag, 8. April 2025, lag in meinem Briefkasten ein amtliches Formular der Hausverwaltung Brunnmatt AG, lose zwischen der Werbung und ohne Couvert. Darauf wird für meine 3,5-Zimmer-Wohnung an der Lindenstrasse 14 in Bern ab dem 1. Juli 2025 eine Nettomiete von CHF 1'645.00 statt der bisherigen CHF 1'480.00 verlangt.

Die Verwaltung beruft sich auf eine amtliche Veröffentlichung zum herangezogenen Satz beziehungsweise zur Berechnungstabelle; einen Auszug daraus führt sie nach eigenen Angaben in ihren Akten. Zu Gesicht bekommen habe ich dieses Blatt nie, und ich weiss weder, was darin steht, noch für welchen Zeitraum es gelten soll.

Aus dem Gedächtnis kann ich sagen: Als Datum trägt das Formular den 14. März 2025, im Begründungsfeld ist von einem Referenzzinssatz von 1,75 Prozent die Rede, und der neue Betrag ist mit CHF 1'645.00 beziffert. Mehr als ein rasches Überfliegen war mir bisher nicht möglich; das Blatt liegt weiterhin bei mir im Ordner.

Im Februar liess mir die Verwaltung eine Berechnungsaufstellung zur Ausgangslage der Miete zukommen, datiert auf den 21. Februar 2025. Wenig später hiess es am Telefon, die dortigen Zahlen zur Ausgangsmiete und zum Ausgangszinssatz seien falsch erfasst und inzwischen berichtigt worden.

An der Hausversammlung vom 12. November 2024 war von rund CHF 40'000.00 wertvermehrendem Anteil an der Küchen- und Badsanierung die Rede, so jedenfalls habe ich es mir damals notiert. Heute stellt sich die Verwaltung auf den Standpunkt, die Kostenaufstellung zu dieser Sanierung weise deutlich mehr als CHF 50'000.00 als wertvermehrend aus; beides zusammen geht nicht auf.

Geprüft haben möchte ich, ob die Erhöhung auf den 1. Juli 2025 überhaupt rechtzeitig und ordnungsgemäss zustande gekommen ist. Offen bleibt für mich vor allem, wann der Inhalt des Formulars tatsächlich fertiggestellt wurde und von welchen Ausgangswerten die Verwaltung dabei ausgegangen ist.

Before the present question can be decided, three points have to be settled: the date carried by the signed increase form, the exact rate or calculation table it relies on together with the period for which that rate or table was in force, and the moment at which the final content of the form was actually prepared. A party's description or recollection of a document does not establish what that document says; the record itself, or the authenticated export, is required.

The starting calculation basis linked to this notice must likewise be established before the current decision is taken. Only the calculation worksheet setting out the starting basis used for the notice will serve this purpose. Figures reported from memory by the tenant or repeated by the manager do not establish that basis; obtain the worksheet itself, or the authenticated export.

A renovation cost breakdown may enter the picture, but only once the notice itself discloses a renovation as the reason for the increase. Unless a returned signed increase notice or form reports that circumstance, the renovation cost breakdown supporting a value-added increase is not to be requested at this stage.

Oktober 2025 einen Nettomietzins von CHF 1'785 statt der bisherigen CHF 1'640 verlangt. Der Umschlag trug keinen Poststempel, und auf dem Formular selbst steht als Datum der 8. September 2025, unterzeichnet von Frau R. Zbinden.

In einem Telefonat vom 15. September 2025 sagte mir ein Mitarbeiter der Verwaltung, der beglaubigte Systemauszug zum Mandat zeige, dass der Formularinhalt erst am 11. September fertiggestellt worden sei; daran erinnere ich mich deutlich, weil ich mir die Uhrzeit notiert habe. Frau Zbinden bestreitet das inzwischen und stellt sich auf den Standpunkt, derselbe Auszug weise für Formular, Tabellenbezug und Bearbeitungsverlauf durchwegs den 8. September 2025 aus. Beide Darstellungen können nicht zugleich zutreffen.

Noch vor diesem Anruf habe ich auf der Publikation des Bundesamts für Wohnungswesen nachgesehen, weil mich der genannte Zinssatz stutzig machte. Soweit ich es im Kopf habe, stand dort, der hypothekarische Referenzzinssatz betrage seit dem 2. Juni 2025 1.75 Prozent und gelte bis zur nächsten Bekanntgabe. Ausdrucken konnte ich die Seite damals nicht, ich gebe die Angabe also aus der Erinnerung wieder.

Bitte prüfen Sie für mich, ob die Erhöhung auf den 1. Oktober 2025 überhaupt greifen kann, nachdem das Formular erst am 12. September bei mir eingetroffen ist. Unklar bleibt mir vor allem, welcher Zeitpunkt zählt: das Datum auf dem Papier oder jener Tag, an dem der Text tatsächlich fertig war. Ebenso wenig verstehe ich, wie sich der Aufschlag von CHF 145 aus der genannten Zinssatzänderung ergeben soll.

Three points belong on the record before the present question is decided: the date on which the increase form was signed, the exact rate or calculation table relied upon together with the period for which it applies, and the moment at which the completed form content was prepared. Two routes establish them: the signed increase notice showing its own date and the rate or table it invokes, combined with the publication excerpt for that rate or table and its effective period, combined with the workflow or audit log recording when the completed form content was prepared; or, alternatively, the authenticated administrative export covering the notice, the table reference and the preparation history. What either side remembers or reports about such a record does not establish its content, so obtain the document itself or the authenticated export.

The starting calculation basis tied to this notice must likewise be on the record beforehand. It is established by the calculation worksheet setting out the basis that was actually used for the notice, showing the reference values it started from. An account of that worksheet given by a party, however confident, does not establish what it contains; the document itself, or an authenticated export of it, is required.

A breakdown of renovation costs is a conditional obligation, not a standing one. It becomes live only if a returned signed increase notice itself reports a renovation as a ground for the increase; for as long as no such ground appears in the notice, do not ask the property manager for the renovation cost breakdown.

Current rent-payment receipts lie outside this check and are not to be requested for it. Readiness here means that the listed facts are established by the documents named above; it does not settle whether the increase is legally owed.

Juni 2025 wurde der Satz von 1.50 auf 1.75 Prozent festgesetzt. Er gilt ab dem 2. Juni 2025 und bleibt bis zur nächsten Bekanntgabe vom 1. Dezember 2025 massgebend.

paragraphs.text: The rent adjustment notice from Brunner Immobilien Treuhand, dated 12 March 2025, landed in my letterbox on 17 March and tells me that the net rent for my flat at Rosenweg 12 in Bern climbs from CHF 1,480 to CHF 1,648 as of 1 July 2025. What jumped out at me straight away is the starting index they worked from: 98.6 points, a figure belonging to December 2015, although I moved in on 1 May 2021 and my lease names the index standing at 100.4 points at that time.

When I looked the index table up on the statistics office pages around the middle of March, the February 2025 value was shown as 106.8 points and I noted it down that way. Going back to the same publication a few days later, February read 106.3 points, with a remark that the earlier release had been revised, and now I genuinely do not know which of the two versions the increase was built on.

I have found the signed increase notice itself; it was sitting in the folder with my lease papers at home, and I can put it in the post or upload it the moment you tell me where it should go. I would rather not retell what it says from memory, because the exact wording seems to matter here and I do not want to garble it.

On 24 March I rang Mr Estermann at the management office, and he explained over the phone that a slice of the increase comes from the bathroom and kitchen works finished in autumn 2024, something like CHF 96,000 all in, with a bit more than half of that counted as value-adding. That is purely what I heard him say down the line; no cost sheet has ever passed through my hands, so I cannot stand behind those figures myself.

What I am asking you to check is whether the increase was calculated from the right starting index and whether the arithmetic holds up at all. The part that stays murky for me is which version of the index table was actually in force when the notice was drawn up, and whether a renovation surcharge is even permitted to ride on top of an index adjustment in the same step.

Over the weekend I went through my tenancy folder and the signed increase form itself is here in the flat, still in the envelope it arrived in. I can drop it off at your office or post you a copy this week if you tell me where it should go.

There is also the letter about the building works from last spring, the one full of figures, which I put aside at the time. Honestly, I can no longer say whether it came from the owner or from the management office, or whether it is the same paper the management already showed you.

In April the management printed out their processing history for the notice for me, and a few weeks later someone there admitted on the phone that the timestamps and numbers in it were wrong and that a corrected listing would be sent. I never followed up to see whether the newer listing says something different.

What I would like looked into is whether the increase was worked out from the right starting index at all, and whether the form was properly drawn up before it went out. What I genuinely cannot work out for myself is which index month they took as their basis, because nothing in the correspondence spells it out.
